dropped.item: Secondary goal: preserve match quality, so replacements meet qualification, availability, location, and client-preference requirements
Secondary goal: keep clients and caregivers informed automatically so no one has to chase status
Secondary goal: give coordinators visibility into what the system did and why, with an easy way to override
Non-goal: replacing coordinators or removing their ability to override decisions
Non-goal: long-term schedule optimization or forecasting of call-outs
Non-goal: handling planned absences such as vacations or scheduled leave
Coordinators should only step in for exceptions, not for routine reassignments
The pilot informs the decision on broader rollout
Examples of care clients depend on: medication, meals, mobility, personal care
Specific work coordinators are pulled away from: planning, onboarding, client communication
Manual rescheduling is hardest to do well when call-outs cluster
Outcomes vary by time of day and call-out volume, not only by coordinator
Agency costs include client retention risk, overtime, and poorly matched assignments
Sunrise Home Care is identified as 'our pilot partner' in the problem statement, and Sunrise handles each case individually
Targets are to be set from the baseline or confirmed; the edit replaces this with 'TBD'

changed.item: Success metrics are presented as defined success metrics in the original but as 'some potential metrics that we could measure' in the edit, which weakens the commitment
Metric 'median time from call-out to confirmed replacement' became 'median time from callout to affected visits being rescheduled', which could include escalations
'Several visits are at risk at once' became 'coordinators need to solve a number of callouts at the same time', shifting from multiple visits to multiple call-outs
Trigger broadened from 'calls in sick' to 'calls out for the day (because they are sick, for example)'
Goal 1 is now 'Automatically reschedule all affected visits', adding 'automatically' and 'all'
Goal 2 is now 'Significantly decrease' coordinator work, instead of 'reduce'
Coordinator impact strengthened from 'pulls them away from' other work to 'inability for coordinators to focus on other tasks'
